questions.prompt: Who is this application for?
questions.help: Pick the choice that fits you best. You can change it later.

questions.prompt: What kind of help are you looking for right now?
questions.help: Pick the one you need most. You can add more later.

questions.prompt: In your own words, what would help the most?
questions.help: A short sentence is fine. This is only to help us point you the right way.

questions.prompt: Which state do you live in?
questions.help: Rules change by state. Pick the state where you sleep most nights.

questions.prompt: Which county or city area do you live in?
questions.help: Your local office depends on this. Not sure? You can leave it blank.

questions.prompt: How many people do you buy and share food with?
questions.help: Count yourself and everyone you live with, even kids. Enter a number.

questions.prompt: How many of those people are under 18?
questions.help: Enter a number. Enter 0 if there are no children.

questions.prompt: How many people in your household are 60 or older?
questions.help: Enter a number. Enter 0 if none.

questions.prompt: Where does money come from for your household?
questions.help: Pick every source that fits. Pick 'none' if there is no money coming in.

options.label: Benefits like disability or retirement checks
No money coming in right now

questions.prompt: What kind of income do you have?
questions.help: This decides which money questions come next. Pick the one that fits best. You can also say you are not sure — then we will ask the general questions.

options.label: I work for myself right now, in my own business or LLC
I had a job before, but I do not work there anymore
Both — I work for myself now and had a job before

questions.prompt: Want to bring in your recent bank and payment statements to show this income?
questions.help: You can share statement files from your bank or payment service, or type the numbers yourself. Anything you share stays on this device, encrypted — nothing is sent anywhere from here. Saying not sure is fine; we will ask for the numbers in a way that works for you.

options.label: I will type the numbers myself

questions.prompt: Do you still work for that earlier employer?
questions.help: Money from a job you no longer have may be treated differently from money you earn now — the office decides. This can help show that old pay is not current income.

options.label: No, I do not work there anymore

questions.prompt: In what month and year did you last get paid by that employer?
questions.help: For example: March 2025. Your best memory is fine. This helps show that the pay is from the past, not current income.

questions.prompt: About how much money comes in from jobs each time you get paid?
questions.help: Your best guess is fine. You can say 'not sure' if you don't know.

questions.prompt: How often does that job money come in?
questions.help: Pick how often the paychecks arrive.

questions.prompt: About how much comes in from benefits each month?
questions.help: This means things like disability or retirement checks. A guess is fine.

questions.prompt: How often does that benefits money come in?
questions.help: Pick how often the checks arrive.

questions.prompt: About how much other money comes in each month?
questions.help: Money from family or friends, child support, or anything else. A guess is fine.

questions.prompt: Where did you sleep last night?
questions.help: Answer honestly. This helps us find the right help, and it does not count against you.

options.label: Outdoors or in a place not meant for sleeping
In a place I rent or own

questions.prompt: How much do you pay for housing each month?
questions.help: Rent or mortgage, if you pay one. Enter 0 if you don't pay for housing.

questions.prompt: How much do you pay for utilities each month?
questions.help: Lights, heat, water, or cooking gas. Enter 0 if you don't pay any.

questions.prompt: How much do you pay for child care each month?
questions.help: Day care, a babysitter, or after-school care. Enter 0 if you don't pay for child care.

questions.prompt: How much do you pay for medical costs each month?
questions.help: Medicine, copays, rides to the doctor. Enter 0 if none. A guess is fine.

questions.prompt: Do you have a photo ID right now?
questions.help: Any government photo ID counts. It is okay if you lost it or never had one. We can still help.

options.label: No, I need to get one
I am working on replacing it

questions.prompt: Tell us what happened to your ID, if you'd like.
questions.help: For example: lost, stolen, or never had one. This is optional. It helps us plan next steps with you.

questions.prompt: What is your date of birth?
questions.help: A guess is okay if you are not sure of the exact day.

questions.prompt: How would you describe your citizenship or immigration status?
questions.help: This question is private and stays on our secure server. Many kinds of help do not depend on this answer, and some programs help family members with different statuses. Pick 'not sure' if you'd rather not say or don't know.

options.label: Not sure / prefer not to say

questions.prompt: Does anyone in your household have a disability or a health condition that limits daily life?
questions.help: This can open extra kinds of help. Pick 'not sure' if you don't know.

questions.prompt: Are you in school or training right now?
questions.help: College, job training, GED classes — any of these count.

questions.prompt: Have you ever served in the military?
questions.help: Any branch, any length of service. Veterans may qualify for extra help.

questions.prompt: Have you gotten help from a benefits office before?
questions.help: Now or in the past, in any state. This does not affect whether you can get help now.

questions.prompt: Where can you get mail?
questions.help: Pick the safest option that works for you. Many people get mail without a home address.

options.label: A shelter or program where I stay

questions.prompt: Has the shelter agreed to hold mail for you?
questions.help: Some shelters only hold mail if you ask them first. Say yes only if you are sure they agreed.

questions.prompt: How do you want us to reach you?
questions.help: Pick what works best for you. This does not have to be a phone.

questions.prompt: What is a phone number where messages can reach you?
questions.help: A friend's number or a shelter number is fine if it works. This stays on our secure server.

questions.prompt: What is your email address?
questions.help: A free email account works if you don't have one. This stays on our secure server.

questions.prompt: When is the best time to reach you?
questions.help: Pick the time you are most likely to be free.

questions.prompt: Are you or anyone applying for Medicaid in one of these situations?
questions.help: Check all that apply. If one applies, you may not need to report work activities for that person — the state decides what counts.

options.label: A parent of a child under 18
A non-parent caregiver of a child under 14, such as a relative or anyone who provides at least 80 hours of care per month
A caregiver of someone who needs help with daily activities, such as a disabled person or an older adult
Already required to meet SNAP or TANF work requirements

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying pregnant now, or have they been in the past 12 months?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying in a treatment program for a drug or alcohol disorder?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Does anyone applying have a drug or alcohol disorder that makes it hard to work? This includes people who have been in recovery for less than 5 years.
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Does anyone applying have a physical, intellectual, or developmental disability that makes it hard to work and do daily activities (such as eating, walking, or getting out of a bed or chair)?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Does anyone applying have a mental health disorder that makes it hard to work (such as schizophrenia, major depression, bipolar disorder, or panic disorder)?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Does anyone applying have a serious health condition that makes it hard to work (such as cancer, multiple sclerosis, HIV/AIDS, or viral hepatitis)?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying in jail or prison now, or were they in the past 4 months?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Was anyone applying in foster care at age 18, and are they now younger than 26?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying a disabled veteran with a 100% disability rating?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Did any of these situations apply last month, but not this month?
questions.help: A situation that applied last month may still matter for what gets reported. The state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Which situations applied last month, but not this month?
questions.help: Check every situation that applied last month but not this month.

options.label: Pregnancy now or in the past 12 months
A parent of a child under 18
A non-parent caregiver of a child under 14
A caregiver of someone who needs help with daily activities
Already meeting SNAP or TANF work requirements
In a treatment program for a drug or alcohol disorder
A drug or alcohol disorder making work hard
A physical, intellectual, or developmental disability
Jail or prison in the past 4 months
Traveling an hour or more for medical care

questions.prompt: Does anyone applying travel an hour or more to get medical care for themselves or a dependent with a serious health condition (including travel coordination that makes it hard to work)?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying receiving care in a hospital for more than 24 hours, or a similar level of care at another location (such as a nursing facility, psychiatric hospital, clinic, the VA, or at home)?
questions.help: You can skip this if you'd rather not answer — the state decides what counts.

questions.prompt: Is anyone applying enrolled as a student (college, vocational, or GED program) full-time or at least half-time?
questions.help: Part-time students can report their hours under work activities instead.

questions.prompt: Does your household make at least $580 in monthly income? This includes all jobs, gig work, seasonal work, and unearned income such as unemployment.
questions.help: Income from seasonal work can be averaged across 6 months. We may match this for you from the income you already gave us — you can always correct it.

questions.prompt: Who completed work activities last month?
questions.help: Report work activities for household members who completed at least 80 hours last month. First names or nicknames are fine.

questions.prompt: What kinds of work activities did they do last month?
questions.help: Check all that apply. Total hours can be a combination of the types of activities listed.

options.label: Community service or unpaid work, including volunteering with a non-profit, school, or other organization, or work in exchange for housing, meals, or other goods
Part-time student hours, where class, lab, or training time counts

questions.prompt: About how many hours of work activities were completed last month?
questions.help: The monthly target is 80 hours. For part-time students, 1 credit hour equals 13 work activity hours per month. A best count is fine.
